notes: Background: Mid-market SaaS that provides conversational workflows for B2B customer support (ticket triage, agent assist, automated followups).

Why Redwood: migrating due to repeated latency regressions with incumbent (started Nov 2025) that impacted streaming UX; interested in hosted API first, then Dedicated for predictable capacity and isolation.

Primary requirement: streaming-first experience for chat agents + tool calling integration (calendar, CRM lookups). Hard SLO: first-byte streaming <= 150ms median; 95th percentile ideally < 400ms for streaming chunks.

Current incumbent: using large-provider API (contracted via partner). Observed regression: median stream first-byte jumped from ~80ms to ~220ms in Nov 2025 during their infra change; customer-visible stuttering and reconnects.

POC objective: benchmark Redwood streaming vs incumbent on our representative flows (10 concurrent agents sim, multimodal tool calls). Focus metrics: median RTFB, 95p chunk latency, token/sec throughput, tool-callback success rate, percent of sessions with stall >500ms.

Redwood early results (internal POC run 2026-02-20): median RTFB 62ms, 95p chunk latency 118ms, tool callback success 99.7%, session stalls >500ms = 0.8% (baseline). Incumbent (same test harness): median RTFB 210ms, 95p chunk latency 430ms, tool callback success 98.2%, session stalls >500ms = 6.3%.
Quote from Taylor: "streaming needs to be consistent — spikes kill agent confidence and increase handle time. If Redwood holds at POC numbers, this is a no-brainer."

Security: SOC2 required; prefer VPC or Private Dedicated for PII-sensitive transcripts. KMS integration needed for customer keying. Data residency requirement: EU for EU customers; currently evaluating whether hosted with regional routing suffices.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget but unit economics matter. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations around batching and quantization to reduce per-token cost without harming latency.
Commercial: asking for committed Dedicated price for 2x current peak concurrent agents (estimate 150 concurrent sessions) + optional burst. Want clear overage terms and SLA for latency/availability.
Ops notes: SE-led deep dive scheduled 2026-03-04; need detailed logs from POC (token-level timing, stream chunk sizes). Legal wants vendor security FAQ answered (see drive link).
Potential risks: incumbent early termination fees; data residency gating for EU customers; need encryption-in-transit + at-rest verification from Redwood for Dedicated/VPC.
Stated next actions: finalize benchmark report by 2026-03-03; exec pricing review week of 2026-03-08; procurement kickoff if legal sign-off on residency and termination terms.
